stock_uncle_insight.date_header: 8/12 法人與主力大戶主要買超股票

buyer_groups.group_title: 1. 外資大戶：資金大挪移，狂掃記憶體與傳產，倒貨面板與金融

stocks.description: 肖年仔，你看這華邦電，外資狂掃 3.78 萬張！這擺明是看好記憶體景氣要翻身，低檔布局，準備等著拉高出貨啦！
至上也被外資買超 3.3 萬張，這跟華邦電一樣，都是記憶體相關的，外資這波是鐵了心要卡位記憶體復甦行情，韭菜們別傻傻去接面板刀啊！
中鋼這檔傳產龍頭，外資也買了 2.92 萬張。這顯示部分資金在電子股高檔震盪時，會轉往相對穩健的傳產股避險，或是看好原物料後市。
外資買超第一金 2.37 萬張，但同時又大賣其他金控股。這操作很賊，可能是對沖避險，或是挑特定金控做波段，不是全面看好金融喔！
0050 被外資買超 1.85 萬張，這很明顯是避險盤，大盤不確定性高，買ETF是最保險的作法，進可攻退可守，穩穩賺大盤的錢。

buyer_groups.group_title: 2. 投信大戶（本土國家隊）：季底作帳秀，狂拉金控股

stocks.description: 投信狂買台新新光金 1.02 萬張，這就是典型的季底作帳行情啦！基金經理人為了績效，會把持股拉高，讓帳面數字好看，肖年仔別傻傻追高啊！
華南金也被投信買超 6.09 千張，跟台新新光金一樣，都是金控股，投信這波就是鎖定金融股在作帳，想跟單的要小心，作帳完可能就倒貨了。
凱基金也入列，投信買超 5.28 千張。本土國家隊這幾天就是把金融股當提款機，拉高出貨或美化財報，這招老狗變不出新把戲啦！
南亞被投信買超 4.5 千張，這檔塑化股，投信買進可能是在配置傳產部位，或是看好其在電子材料的佈局，但量能不算特別突出。
和碩被投信買超 3.57 千張，這組裝廠，投信買進可能是看好蘋果新機或AI伺服器題材，但也要注意是不是短線操作。

buyer_groups.group_title: 3. 內資主力與實戶：短線避險與低接半導體

stocks.description: 自營商買超聯電 1.39 千張，這檔晶圓代工二哥，外資也買，自營商也買，顯示市場對半導體族群的看法開始轉趨正面，但自營商通常是短線操作，隔日沖的機率不低。
自營商買超 0050 723 張，跟外資一樣，都是在買ETF避險，大盤震盪，先求穩再求賺，這是老手們的共識。
南亞被自營商買超 585 張，這跟投信的動作有點像，可能是在傳產股中尋找相對低基期或有題材的標的，但自營商的量通常不大，短線成分居多。
自營商買超富邦科技 537 張，這檔電子科技ETF，顯示自營商看好電子股的整體表現，但又不想單壓個股，所以選擇ETF來分散風險。
力積電被自營商買超 497 張，這檔記憶體與晶圓代工廠，跟外資買華邦電、南亞科的邏輯類似，都是在低檔布局半導體，但自營商的量小，通常是短打。

strategies.strategy_title: 策略一：外資大戶換股操作，從高檔轉進低基期半導體與傳產
strategies.strategy_content: 肖年仔，你看外資這次操作很明顯，大賣面板雙虎（友達、群創）跟航空股（華航），這些都是之前漲多的股票，現在獲利了結，把資金倒出來。然後呢？他們轉手就去狂掃記憶體（華邦電、至上、南亞科）跟部分晶圓代工（聯電），這擺明是看好半導體產業谷底翻揚，趁現在低基期卡位。同時也買進中鋼、華新等傳產，這是在電子股震盪時，找相對穩健的傳產股避險，或是看好原物料後市，這就是大戶的資金挪移術啦！

strategies.strategy_title: 策略二：投信季底作帳，狂拉金控股美化財報
strategies.strategy_content: 本土國家隊投信，這招老狗變不出新把戲啦！你看他們狂掃台新新光金、華南金、凱基金這些金控股，這就是典型的季底作帳行情。基金經理人為了讓基金淨值好看，會把持股拉高，等財報公布後，這些股票可能就會被倒貨。肖年仔們，別傻傻地去追高，小心被割韭菜！這波金融股的漲勢，很多都是作帳行情撐起來的，要特別留意風險。

strategies.strategy_title: 策略三：內資避險與短線操作，ETF與半導體並重
strategies.strategy_content: 自營商跟部分內資主力，他們的動作通常比較短線。這次他們大賣第一金、面板雙虎，跟外資的賣超方向一致，顯示對這些股票的看法偏空。但他們也買進聯電、力積電等半導體股，跟外資一樣看好半導體。同時，他們也買進元大台灣50和富邦科技這些ETF，這就是典型的避險操作，大盤不確定性高，買ETF可以分散風險，又能參與市場漲勢。這就是短線操作與避險兼顧的策略啦！

stock_uncle_insight.summary: 肖年仔，今天大戶們的動作很清楚，外資在換股，從舊經濟轉新經濟，投信在作帳，狂拉金融股，自營商則在短線避險。記住，跟著大戶走，但別傻傻追高，小心被倒貨！

凱基台北這分點，買聯電 559 張，這量不大，但這家分點是出了名的隔日沖大戶，今天買，明天高機率就倒貨給你，肖年仔別傻傻去接刀啊！
元大投信買超台新新光金 4.59 千張，這就是投信自家券商在幫自家基金作帳啦！拉高股價，美化帳面，等著結帳完就可能放手，這招很常見，韭菜們要看清楚！
摩根大通這外資大咖，大賣友達 1.68 萬張，這跟外資整體大賣面板股的趨勢一致。這代表他們對面板景氣看法悲觀，或是之前已經賺飽飽，現在準備拉高出貨，割韭菜啦！

english_professor_news.title: 億illionaire sues ex-employee over alleged theft

level1_blind.text:
Russell Wilson is the billionaire founder of CoinSpot, one of Australia's largest cryptocurrency trading exchanges. Founded in 2013, CoinSpot reported a $270 million net profit in the 2025 financial year.

On Aug. 10, a local media outlet reported that he has sued an ex-employee for allegedly stealing around $500,000 from the exchange.

The court documents filed by CoinSpot's parent company, Casey Block Services, claim that customer support team member Iresh Pawan Perera moved $478,932 out of the company into his personal bank account across 76 transactions in the two years to March.

The lawsuit claims Perera converted CoinSpot's digital currency for “his own use by exchanging it” into cash. His job was terminated immediately on March 9 because the alleged misappropriation of funds amounted to “material breaches” of his employment agreement. Perera is yet to file a defence.

Wilson's company is seeking damages worth $478,932, in addition to interest. The case will resume in September.

A CoinSpot spokeswoman told the publication that she could not reveal more details about the crypto exchange's legal battle with its ex-employee while the matter is sub judice.

“CoinSpot enforces robust safeguards to ensure operations and assets remain secure,” she said. “We take the security of our customers' holdings extremely seriously and have not had customer funds impacted on our platform. CoinSpot has zero tolerance for fraud and will always work closely with law enforcement to protect our users.”

This story was originally published by TheStreet on Aug 10, 2026, where it first appeared in the MARKETS section. Add TheStreet as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

english_professor_news.title: Bullish Oil Bets Shrink for a Second Week Running, COT Data Show
english_professor_news.level1_blind:
Money managers have reduced their bullish bets on both Brent and WTI crude futures over the past two weeks despite little progress on a potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

In the latest reporting week to August 4, portfolio managers trimmed their net long position in NYMEX WTI by 7,257 lots to 101,050 lots, data from the exchanges found. The net long position, the difference between bullish and bearish bets, in ICE Brent crude oil futures was slashed by 11%, or by 20,361 lots to 164,722 lots.

This was the second consecutive weekly decline in speculative positions in the two key crude oil futures benchmarks as traders and speculators are hesitant to add more bullish bets on a price rally.

Oil prices have dropped over the past two weeks amid hopes that the Strait of Hormuz could reopen and Iran and Oman could reach a deal on a joint management of some of the lanes.

"Speculative sentiment turned more cautious last week," ING's commodities strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey wrote in a note early on Monday.

According to Ole Hansen, Head of Commodity Strategy at Saxo Bank, the energy complex saw reduced exposure in the weekly Commitment of Traders report through August 4 despite persistent supply risks.

"Renewed price weakness drove a 25k reduction in the combined crude net long to 266k contracts, following 171k of net buying during the previous three weeks," Hansen said.

"Despite persistent geopolitical supply risks, positioning continues to signal limited conviction in a sustained price rally," the commodity expert noted.

english_professor_news.title: EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and USD/CAD 舒 Short-Term Forecast for 10/8/2026

level1_blind.text:
The Euro finds itself a little bit soft on Monday as we head into the New York session. I'll be watching the 1.1520 area for potential support. We'll have to wait and see. A little bit of a bounce would be compelling, for me at least, to start thinking about the upside, but if we break down below there, then we could see a deeper correction.

As usual, we'll have to watch the interest rate situation in the United States vis- vis Europe, and at this point, it looks very much like a market that is trying to turn things around from a longer-term standpoint, but one could also make an argument for a little bit of a rising wedge. We'll just have to wait and see.

The British pound has found itself a little bit soft as well, not horribly so, as we are still very much in consolidation near the 1.35 level. If we were to break down below the 1.3475 level, then we could start to think about challenging that explosive candlestick after the non-farm payroll announcement on Friday.

Nonetheless, this is a market in which the pound has fared better against the U.S. dollar than many other currencies over the last couple of years, due to the fact that the interest rates in the U.K. are elevated. So, if I get an option between buying Euros or pounds today on a bounce, for myself, I may actually favor the pound.

The U.S. dollar is rising a bit against the Canadian dollar after forming a bit of a double bottom. This is a market that has been rounding from a huge move to the upside. We are currently at the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement level, followed by the 50% retracement level, trying to find some type of floor. Ultimately, this is a market that is an interest rate differential play as well. There are some traders out there that are off to the races when it comes to the idea of the U.S. employment situation dropping, but one errant report really doesn't make a trend.

Furthermore, unfortunately, the Canadian jobs numbers, although really hot this month, are notorious for being horribly wrong and corrected the next time. So, we can't read too much into one report, and I think we're starting to see people question that. The interest rate differential pays traders to hold the U.S. dollar versus the Canadian dollar. I think eventually that comes back into play, especially with a 55% chance of the Federal Reserve raising rates in September.
